gloss: way one uses one's hands; hand movements

definitions.gloss: way one uses one's hands; hand movements
definitions.explanation: The visible manner in which someone moves their hands while doing something. Almost always used with a modifier that judges the movement as skilled, clumsy, gentle, and so on.

examples.japanese: ⟦{慣|な}れた→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧{手|て}つき⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧さばく。
examples.english: To fillet a fish with practiced hands.

examples.japanese: {危|あぶ}なっかしい{手|て}つき⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包丁|ほうちょう}→包丁：04976_houchou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}っている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: He is using the kitchen knife with an alarmingly clumsy grip.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{優|やさ}しい{手|て}つき⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{抱|だ}き{上|あ}げ、⟦そっと→そっと：03321_sotto⟧⟦{布団|ふとん}→布団：01720_futon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{寝|ね}かせた→寝かせる：12322_nekaseru⟧。
examples.english: She picked the baby up with gentle hands and laid it softly on the futon.

notes:
Nearly always appears as 「{modifier}な{手|て}つき⟦で→で：00502_de⟧」 describing how an action is performed. It is about the look of the movement, not about the hands themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{慣|な}れた→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧{手|て}つき: practiced, assured hand movements
- {危|あぶ}なっかしい{手|て}つき: clumsy, unsafe-looking handling
- {優|やさ}しい{手|て}つき: gentle hands
- ⟦{鮮|あざ}やか→鮮やか：05702_azayaka⟧な{手|て}つき: deft, impressive handling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{手|て}さばき→手さばき：30146_tesabaki⟧: handling, dexterity — emphasizes technique and speed, typically praising skill
- ⟦{仕草|しぐさ}→仕草：10917_shigusa⟧: gesture, mannerism — any bodily movement or habit, not limited to the hands
